figures.caption: Fig. 1 (a) Ordered crystal structure of Li6PS5X (X ¼ Cl, Br, I). The X anions form a cubic close-packed lattice with PS4 tetrahedra in the octahedral sites and free S2 in half of the tetrahedral sites (Wyckoﬀ4d). (b) The Li+ cages-like polyhedra in which diﬀerent jump processes are possible: (i) doublet jumps between adjacent lithium positions (48h–24g–48h), intra-cage jumps within the cage (48h–48h), and inter-cage jumps between the cages (48h–48h). figures.caption: Fig. 3 Structural data for Li6+xP1xSixS5Br obtained from the Rietveld reﬁnements of the XRD patterns. (a) Lattice parameters increased with an increase in x due to the larger ionic radius of Si4+. The upper limit in the lattice parameter at a composition of x ¼ 0.3 is limited by the solubility. (b) MS4 (M ¼ Si1xPx) polyhedral volumes increased due to the Si4+ substitution and resultant unit-cell expansion. (c) Site disorder between Br and S2, which is relatively constant as x increases. The error bars reﬂect 3s of the standard deviations obtained from the Rietveld reﬁnement. Reproduced with permission from ref. 27. Copyright 2018, the Royal Society of Chemistry.

figures.caption: Fig. 4 (a) Crystal structure of Li6.7Si0.7Sb0.3S5I with fully occupied S (16e) site and 2.6% and 1.7% S2/I (4a, 4c) mixed occupied sites. The dark violet polyhedron indicates the (Sb/Si)S4 tetrahedra. The colored balls indicate four Li+ sites: turquoise (Li1, 48h), teal (Li2, 24g), green (Li3, 48h), and orange (Li, 4d). (b) Discrete jumps of Li+ diﬀusion: doublet jumps (Li1 (48h)–Li2 (24g)–Li1 (48h): blue arrow), intra-cage jumps (Li1 (48h)–Li1 (48h): red arrow), and inter-cage jumps (Li1 (48h)– Li1 (48h): orange arrow); (c) the new inter-cage jump Li3 (48h)–Li3 (48h) (orange arrow). Reproduced with permission from ref. 85. Copyright 2019, American Chemical Society.
